recipes.name: Moo Goo Gai Pan II
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) can sliced water chestnuts, drained
salt and black pepper to taste
0.75 cup skinless, boneless chicken breast meat - thinly sliced

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Stir in the mushrooms, snow peas, water chestnuts, and bok choy; season to taste with salt and pepper. Cook and stir until the vegetables are just tender, about 5 minutes. Remove the vegetables from the wok and wipe the wok clean.

Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in the wok. Stir in the garlic and ginger; cook a few seconds until the garlic begins to turn golden brown. Stir in the chicken and cook until the chicken is no longer pink, about 5 minutes. Add the wine, sugar, and chicken broth; bring to a boil. Dissolve the cornstarch in the water and stir into the simmering sauce. Once the sauce returns to a simmer, stir until thick and clear, about 30 seconds. Return the vegetables to the wok and toss until hot and coated with the sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Moo Goo Gai Pan II
raw_recipe.description: Snow peas, bok choy, and water chestnuts join chicken in this take-out favorite.

review.reviewBody: This turned out verrrry good, I was scared to be the first to try it but I am glad that I did. My grandma always orders moo goo gai pan when we eat out at chinese, so I wanted to try this recipe out and hopefully surprise her one day! I think she will be happily surprised with this one! I did change the veggies up a little bit to my liking and how it's served at our local chinese place. I added a head of broccoli and a can of stir fry corn. I left out the bok choy and used bamboo shoots in place of the water chestnuts. I used frozen peas and they worked just fine. For the sauce I did use powdered ginger and a little more than 1/2 cup of chicken broth. I had some cooking white wine that I've had forever but it didn't seem to ruin anything. I added about 1 tbls of soy sauce just because, not really sure why. Me and my mom both enjoyed this, will make again. Thanks for the great recipe.

Delicious! I used chicken tenderloins, making it really easy to slice. My grocer was out of snow peas, so I used sugar snap peas instead. Everything else stayed exactly according to recipe, although I doubled it. Such an easy, healthy, and good recipe! Next time I think I will add something to give it some heat like red pepper flakes.

It was delicious! I used beef instead of chicken for a change. So used beef broth, and doubled the sauce with a sprinkle of pepper flakes for a little zing. . I also used a little regular cabbage to replace the Bock Choy and a chopped onion. A word of caution. Wait a few minutes into the sauté before adding the snow peas or they will loose their beautiful color and texture. Sprinkled in some carrot sticks at the end. I will make it again!

My first time making moo goo gai pan. It was absolutely fantastic. Just like I would expect from a restaurant. Because of the amount of prep work needed. did my measuring and prep work the day before I was ready to make my meal.

I liked the essence of this recipe. This was a great homemade version of Chinese takeout. I used two large chicken breasts, added some zucchini to the vegetables and quadrupled the sauce recipe because I like a lot of sauce and it seemed like I had a lot of chicken and vegetables. I added about a tablespoon of soy sauce to my sauce and then only doubled the cornstarch thickener. I forgot to start my ginger and garlic getting fragrant, but I think I preferred adding it with my chicken rather than the times I have cooked it the other way when making this recipe before. We ended up with 5+ hearty servings of this.

great recipe! swapped out bok choy and snow peas for celery, carrots, onions and also added some cashews. doubled the sauce cuz I had a lot of veggies and was pretty happy how this turned out. next time will try with bamboo shoots, mushrooms and snow peas. sauce couldve had a bit more kick, added soy sauce after but will maybe tinker more next time.

We really liked it. I added fresh bean sprouts, sliced onion & subbed celery for bok choy. I added a little soy sauce to the finished dish because it needed a little more salt. I also used pheasant instead of chicken. Will make again.

My husband and I both liked this recipe a lot. It's different than the spicy Chinese food we usually favor. I followed the recipe with the exception of substituting matchstick carrots for the mushrooms and a large slivered red onion for the water chestnuts. I served it on hot rice. Immediately, my older son came to join us for dinner. You may want to double up on the sauce, but I liked how it just coated the vegetables. Oh...and go heavy on the garlic and fresh ginger!
This was a very good base MGGP recipe. If you want to spice it up a little, add 1/2 teaspoon or more of chili garlic sauce. That will kick up the spice level.
This tasted bland as written. I ended up adding some soy sauce to give it a kick before serving.

This very good and easy dish, used a bag of frozen snap peas, carrots, mushrooms and water chestnuts and added extra snap peas. Added thinly sliced carrots and celery. I didn’t have chicken broth, so dissolved half bouillon chicken cube which added very good flavor. Added a little extra rice wine in place of white wine. Since I love ginger and garlic added probably two teaspoons.
Just like the restaurant version I love. This recipe isn't meant to be spicy. I made as is but it would be good with different vegetables if you didn't have these on hand.

This turned out amazing! My family loved the flavors and it was such a simple recipe to follow. I substituted the vegetables with ones I already had on hand (asparagus, onions, and mini bell peppers), and it worked out wonderfully. I’ll definitely be making this again.
Delicious
Great!! I added homemade fried rice!
This recipe’s flavor was a bit too subtle for our taste. I made it as written and I doubled the sauce but it was very bland. I will not make it again.

I bought fresh veg from the farmers market and wanted a white sauce. The sauce here was so simple and I had everything on hand. The family liked it. When I was making supper another day I got this out and it was good cold.
SOOOOO good as is! I added jalepenos to add spice, otherwise unchanged.
No msg. Yummy
Delicious! Only change I made was to add a chopped onion to the mix. Consistency was spot on. Next time I'll try the brown sauce version.
